# Configured cron jobs reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/maintenance/generate-cron-reference.ts. Edit the executable sources, then regenerate. -->

Run `npm run cron:reference` to regenerate; `npm run cron:reference:check` fails when this file is stale. The generator reads executable registry keys and worker lease calls through the TypeScript AST, and imports only the pure schedule, freshness, financial-name and manual-only catalogs. The freshness line is the `/api/health/jobs` budget derived from the schedule in [lib/cron/operational-health.ts](../../lib/cron/operational-health.ts); `paging` jobs make the probe answer 503 when overdue. It never imports worker modules or contacts a database or vendor.

## Inventory and evidence

- **81 registered cleanup jobs:** 81 configured ticker targets and 0 registered jobs outside the ticker.
- **Configured is not live-verified.** Every row describes repository configuration. This generation did not check deployment state, accepted Sentry check-ins or completed obligations. The fleet switch selects the active platform; a configured ticker target is not proof that it executed.
- **12 targets per tick is a tested wave design bound.** The resumable ledger target yields on crowded slots; other due work is not truncated. The cadence/collision tests guard the planned roster. An HTTP abort does not cancel the worker, and a lease does not deduplicate sequential external effects.

## Registered jobs

The purpose column expands imported entry function names, not a second hand-maintained policy description. Core links are statically visible worker imports; inline implementations link to their registry entry. Lease lookup follows local imports by at most two levels and reports unresolved metadata explicitly. Lease fields show configured mode/TTL, not proof of successful acquisition. Default TTL is declared in [lib/cron/with-cron-lock.ts](../../lib/cron/with-cron-lock.ts); maintenance admission comes from [lib/cron/financial-jobs.ts](../../lib/cron/financial-jobs.ts). The idle probe column names the claim-predicate probe the ticker runs before dispatch ([lib/cron/idle-probe.ts](../../lib/cron/idle-probe.ts)); a job with no work on a due tick is skipped and recorded on the tick's claim row, and an always-run job states why it has no probe.

## Changing a job

1. Keep one implementation and register its cleanup builder; do not add wrapper layers.
2. Update [lib/cron/schedule.ts](../../lib/cron/schedule.ts) for ticker timing and request limits. Preserve one active schedule.
3. Regenerate this reference and run the schedule/collision, inventory and documentation drift tests.
4. Verify completed work and error/hold behavior in the deployed environment before treating the configuration as healthy. Record deployment evidence separately from this generated file.

## Deprecated & Superseded Approaches

Manual inventory counts, marker-comment scraping and copied schedule tables drifted from the executable roster. This file now derives builder keys, schedule values, worker imports and lease declarations from source. Generated configuration cannot replace a deployed recovery/failback check, a backlog measurement or accepted monitoring events. No additional scheduler, job-control table or worker-importing JobSpec is introduced.
